answer: A market can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, with the stake growing toward its summit only after a history of honest deals. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, and a gale of complaints backed by evidence slashes them all at once. New identities start at the zenith of suspicion and earn trust slowly, so an attacker pays real money for every fake face while honest agents keep their deposit.
